probe:citations-api.summary:
Custom tools can return page-level citations. The tool_result for read_pages can hold search_result blocks with citations enabled. This is part of the standard Messages API, needs no beta header, and works on claude-opus-5. The docs say "All active models support search results with citations, with the exception of Claude Haiku 3. No beta header is required" (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/search-results).

Block shape: {type:"search_result", source:<any stable string>, title, content:[{type:"text", text (non-empty)}...], citations:{enabled:true}, cache_control?}.

Limits:
- Text only.
- If a tool_result contains any search_result block, all its blocks must be search_result.
- Citations must be on for every search_result in the request or off for all; mixing is an error.
- search_result blocks may appear only in user turns.
- A whole text block is the smallest citable unit, so split each page into paragraph blocks.

Each citation comes back on the answer's text blocks as {type:"search_result_location", cited_text, source, title, search_result_index, start_block_index, end_block_index (exclusive)}. The answer is split into many text blocks, and only the cited spans carry citations. Set source = page_id and read page_id straight from citation.source. Cross-check against search_result_index (it counts every search_result block in the request, across all messages) and against the paragraph blocks that were sent.

Streaming:
- Citations arrive as content_block_delta events with delta type citations_delta, one citation per delta.
- SDK 0.122.0 adds a "citation" helper event with the citation and a snapshot of all citations so far.
- It also collects them into TextBlock.citations, so get_final_message() returns the full lists.

Interactions:
- Prompt caching works with citations. cache_control can go on the search_result block. Turning citations on or off rewrites the system prompt, so the system and message caches are invalidated.
- Structured outputs are incompatible: any citation-enabled document or search_result block plus output_config.format returns a 400 error. The table and compare features must send pages with citations off.
- Adaptive thinking: no documented conflict was found.
- Fallback if search_result could not be used: custom-content document blocks. They produce content_block_location citations with document_index and document_title but no source, and they are all-or-none per request.

Deliverables are citations.md and example_tool_loop.py. The loop compiles, and its offline self-test against a fake HTTP server passed 14 of 14 checks. It was not run against the API.

recommendations: Use search_result blocks in the read_pages tool_result: source=page_id, title='YYYY년치 · 「판 이름」 · N쪽', one text block per paragraph, citations {enabled:true}. Map citations by citation.source and use search_result_index plus cited_text only as a cross-check.

Have search and get_toc return plain strings, so they cannot be cited and Claude must call read_pages before citing. Return read_pages errors as a plain-string tool_result with is_error=true, never mixed with search_result blocks in the same tool_result.
Never send an empty text block (minLength 1). In prep, split page text into paragraphs, and give blank pages a placeholder or skip them.
For the summary feature (§5.2), put the chapter's pages as top-level search_result blocks in the user message, with cache_control on the last block.

For table and compare (§5.3–5.4), which use output_config.format, add a citations on/off switch to read_pages and send every search_result with citations off, or the request gets a 400 error. Keep page_id in each row as the spec already plans.

In the loop, re-send final.content unchanged as the assistant turn, which keeps thinking signatures intact. Put tool_result blocks first in the user turn. When a limit is hit, answer pending tool_use blocks with is_error results plus a text instruction, and set tool_choice {type:'none'}; the tools param stays in the request (INF: history with tool_use blocks probably still needs tool definitions).

Make the first paid smoke test a 2-3 turn QA with the default adaptive thinking. Confirm (a) citations and thinking blocks come back in the same response, (b) cache_read_input_tokens on the first request after read_pages, to see whether citations switching on invalidates the cache, (c) the real separator in multi-block cited_text.
In the UI, merge the answer's text blocks into sentences and put [n] markers after cited blocks. Mark only substantive uncited blocks as '근거 없음'; skip short connective fragments.
risks: Cache cost (INF): QA requests before the first read_pages have no citation-enabled blocks. The docs say turning citations on or off rewrites the system prompt, so the switch may rewrite the system and message caches once per question.
The citations-on/off rule covers the whole request history. A loop or replay that mixes pages sent with citations on and off (for example, reusing a QA transcript for a table task) will fail.
Citation granularity depends on block size: one block per page makes cited_text the whole page. Paragraph splitting quality in prep directly affects the 근거 문장 display.
search_result_index shifts if earlier messages are trimmed or edited; relying on the index instead of source would mis-map citations.
The self-test only proves SDK-side request shape and delta accumulation against a fake server; real server acceptance and model citation behaviour for Korean text are unverified until a paid call.
inferred: Mapping by citation.source = page_id is the most robust choice (source is echoed back verbatim per the docs; that it survives history trimming is inferred).
With every search_result sent with citations off, output_config.format should be accepted (inferred from the wording 'If you enable citations on any user-provided document ... 400').
The first request that contains citation-enabled blocks may count as the 'citations toggle' cache invalidation. Not documented at that level of detail.
Short connective text blocks without citations are normal (doc examples show them), so a length heuristic is needed before marking '근거 없음'.
Keeping the tools param while tool_choice is 'none' for the wrap-up call is the safe pattern when the history contains tool_use blocks. Not verified in docs this session.

probe:hf-spaces.summary:
Checked the official HF docs, the pricing and storage pages, and huggingface_hub source at tag v1.31.0 on 2026-09-14. I pulled 96 key quotes from the live pages and all 96 matched (E = exact after whitespace normalization, L = same wording, only formatting differs). Compact table (URL keys are defined in hf_spaces.md):
1. PRO and sleep. OV: "Gradio and Docker Spaces run on compute and require a paid plan to create: PRO for personal accounts" (E). PR: "Host ZeroGPU, Gradio & Docker Spaces" (E). CPU Basic is 2 vCPU, 16 GB RAM, 50 GB non-persistent disk. GPU: sleeps after "(currently, 48 hours). Anyone visiting your Space will restart it automatically." (E). The sleep time cannot be changed on free hardware.
2. README YAML keys, exact names (CFG): sdk ("gradio"/"docker"/"static"), sdk_version, python_version ("Defaults to 3.10", so set "3.12"), app_file, suggested_hardware ("will not automatically assign" hardware; value "cpu-basic"), startup_duration_timeout (default 30m), disable_embedding. suggested_storage is ignored because persistent storage was removed.
3. Protected (OV, SET): set from the Settings visibility dropdown; PRO only; added 2026-03-18. The repo, including data, is visible only to owner/collaborators; the running app is public at https://<sub>.hf.space. In the API, create_repo and update_repo_settings accept visibility="protected". create_repo ignores it if the repo already exists.
4. Secrets: add them in Settings or with add_space_secret(repo_id, key, value). The app reads them as environment variables (os.getenv). Values are write-only. Variables are public, so the API key must never go there. Any change to secrets restarts the app.
5. Buckets: STO says "Storage Buckets are the recommended way to persist data in your Space". They can be attached at Space creation, in the settings UI, or through the API with Volume(type="bucket", source=..., mount_path="/data"); the path must start with "/" and buckets mount read-write by default. set_space_volumes replaces all volumes. Buckets have no versions and deletes are permanent. They count toward the account quota; PRO includes 1TB private storage, then $18/TB/mo. Fallback: a private dataset repo with CommitScheduler (append-only, every >=5 min, upload errors silently retried).
6. Deploy: create_repo(repo_type="space", space_sdk="gradio"), then upload_folder with allow_patterns/ignore_patterns. Every commit rebuilds the Space. Xet is on by default and upload_folder auto-splits large commits. Hard per-file limit is 500GB. The docs' "no per-repo size limit" covers only models and datasets; a ~1 GB Space repo cap appears only in forum posts, where HF staff wrote "We do not recommend storing data in a Space repo."
7. Outbound: ports 80, 443 and 8080 are allowed; all other ports are blocked.
8. Logs, restart: fetch_space_logs(build=True/follow=True) or `hf spaces logs`; SSE log endpoints need authentication. restart_space(factory_reboot=True) "rebuilt from scratch without caching any requirements". The UI also has a factory reboot button.
9. Terms: HF ToS "You are solely responsible for the Content you post"; the service is as-is and access can be suspended. Anthropic AUP (effective Sept 15, 2025): a public chatbot "must disclose to users that they are interacting with AI". Gradio apps expose an HTTP API, and api_visibility="private" only hides endpoints from the client libraries, so usage limits must be enforced on the server.
Unknowns:
- how bucket volumes on Spaces write (append support, upload timing)
- whether attaching volumes restarts the Space
- any volume limits on CPU Basic
- the official Space repo size cap
- what non-collaborators see at hf.co/spaces/<id> for a Protected Space
- how long waking from sleep takes
- which huggingface_hub version the Space image preinstalls
- how to get the visitor IP behind the proxy
- rate limits on commits
Deliverables: hf_spaces.md and deploy_example.py. The script passes py_compile and was not run; it is a dry run unless --yes is passed.

probe:api-behaviors.summary:
I checked all 9 API topics and wrote 61 claim rows to api_behaviors.md, each with an exact quote and a line-numbered source. Sources were 20 live platform.claude.com doc pages (downloaded to live/), the bundled claude-api skill, and the installed anthropic 0.122.0 source. SDK-side behavior was also tested with httpx.MockTransport: canned local responses, no network and no Anthropic API call. snippets.py passes py_compile and has not been run against the API. Two small offline checks of it did run: the error classifier and cost function on built exceptions, and the SDK's retry and stream handling.

Findings that should change the plan:
(a) The whole tool loop must use client.beta.messages.stream/create/parse with fallbacks="default" and betas=["server-side-fallback-2026-07-01"]. Both are typed parameters; extra_body is not needed. Beta types carry the fallback block and usage.iterations.
(b) A streaming refusal that fires while a tool_use block is still open on the stream is not retried on a fallback model. The UI needs a refusal path anyway.
(c) The SDK retries the monthly spend-cap 429 twice anyway: 3 attempts, about 1.3 s. A user-set spend limit is a 400 and is not retried. To detect it, read e.body['error']['message']; e.message is a repr string.
(d) A mid-stream SSE error arrives as a plain APIStatusError with status_code 200 and .type 'overloaded_error'. It is not an OverloadedError and is not retried.
(e) The non-beta messages.parse has no cache_control argument; beta.messages.parse has cache_control and fallbacks.
(f) Structured outputs cannot be combined with citations (400), and citations must be all on or all off per request. Table and compare requests must not enable citations on any search_result block.
(g) Caches are isolated per workspace, so dev testing will not warm the public workspace's cache.
(h) The Opus 5 cache minimum is 512 tokens. Prices: $5 input, $6.25 5-minute cache write, $10 1-hour write, $0.50 cache read, $25 output. Batch is half of each ($2.50/$12.50), stacking with the cache multipliers.
(i) Batch custom_id must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$ (no Korean). Results come back unordered.

Compact verified table (full quotes are in api_behaviors.md):
1 Fallbacks: "default" form needs header 2026-07-01 (2026-06-01 accepts the list form only). A refusal is HTTP 200 with stop_reason refusal. A refusal before any output is not billed. A fallback shows up as top-level model, a fallback content block, and a fallback_message entry in usage.iterations. Rate limits and 5xx never fall back. Not allowed in batches. Client-side option: BetaRefusalFallbackMiddleware with an explicit model list plus BetaFallbackState; never combine it with fallbacks=.
2 Thinking: on by default on Opus 5 (adaptive). display defaults to "omitted" (the SDK docstring wrongly says summarized). Pass thinking and redacted_thinking blocks back unchanged; keep history append-only. Forced tool_choice works with adaptive thinking. effort goes in output_config.effort, default high. max_tokens caps thinking plus text.
3 Structured outputs: output_config.format is GA and supports Opus 5. additionalProperties must be false. No numeric or string length limits; minItems only 0 or 1. Up to 20 strict tools, 24 optional parameters, 16 union-typed parameters, 180 s compile timeout. Output may break the schema on refusal or max_tokens. messages.parse exists in 0.122.0. strict:true tools are the alternative.
4 Caching: order is tools, then system, then messages. One marker on the system block plus top-level cache_control (automatic caching uses 1 of 4 slots). 20-block lookback. Changing tool_choice only invalidates the messages cache. Cache reads do not count toward ITPM.
5 Streaming: a tool call starts with content_block_start (tool_use, with id and name); input arrives as input_json_delta. The SDK helper yields input_json events with a snapshot, content_block_stop carries the finished block, and get_final_message() returns the full message.
6 Errors: SDK max_retries=2 on connection errors, 408, 409, 429 and 5xx; honors retry-after when 0 < value ≤ 60; backoff 0.5 s doubling, capped at 8 s. Typed classes run from BadRequestError to OverloadedError.
7 Token counting: client.messages.count_tokens hits POST /v1/messages/count_tokens. It is free, returns an estimate, and has its own RPM limit. No Korean ratio is documented; the generic figure is 2.5M characters per 1M tokens. Tool use adds a hidden 286-token system prompt.
8 Pricing: see (h). A fallback to Opus 4.8 is the same price. inference_geo "us" costs 1.1x.
9 Batches: create, then retrieve until processing_status is ended, then results(). Limits: 100k requests or 256 MB; expires at 24 h; results kept 29 days; errored, canceled and expired items are not billed.

Limit wrap-up: do not switch to tool_choice none. It invalidates the message cache on the biggest request and blocks report_status, forcing status 'answered'. Keep tool_choice auto, return is_error for any tool other than report_status, and hard-stop after 1-2 extra turns. Count limits per call so one of two parallel calls can still run.
The '근거 없음' length rule of 8 letters is too high for Korean. Use a lower threshold or a rule based on punctuation and digits.
Summary feature: leave cache_control off the chapter pages unless a follow-up request is planned. A cache write costs 1.25x and is never read.
Source label: the 'Thinking also interleaves with tool use automatically' quote is at build-with-claude/adaptive-thinking L27, not a thinking-steering-and-cost page.
missing: Spec §4.3 fallbacks are beta. The loop must use client.beta.messages.stream(..., betas=['server-side-fallback-2026-07-01'], fallbacks='default') with Beta* types (BetaCitationEvent exists in SDK 0.122.0). Rules from refusals-and-fallback: "The request must be valid as a direct request to every model named" (L634). A `fallback` block must be kept where it appeared, and thinking and tool_use blocks before the final fallback block must be dropped (L700-711), so re-sending final.content unchanged is not always valid. Top-level usage covers only the attempt that served the reply, so cost tracking must sum usage.iterations (L741). A streaming decline while a tool_use block is still open is not retried (L737).
The citations page promises "citations are guaranteed to contain valid pointers to the provided documents", so the index and cited_text cross-check can be a warning-only safety net.

Changing tool_choice invalidates the message cache (prompt-caching table). Also, cached thinking blocks "count as input tokens when read from cache" (thinking L1029), which affects the 200k cumulative-token cap.
Whether search_result and text blocks nested inside a tool_result count toward the 20-position cache lookback is undocumented. Check cache_read_input_tokens on every turn in the first paid test.

Streaming interruptions on Claude 4.6+ models (Opus 5): resume with a user message holding the partial text, not a prefill (streaming L1493-1502). The SDK's 2 retries do not cover a stream that breaks midway; partial citations are lost.
Alternative trade-off: plain-text document blocks are split into sentences automatically (citations page tip) but return document_index instead of source. search_result needs segmentation done by us.
A not_found answer has no citations by nature. The UI or grading needs a rule so it is not greyed out as '근거 없음', and the loop must still allow report_status under limits.

Token overhead per search_result or text block, and any block-count limit, are unknown. Measure with token counting (documented as compatible with citations) on real 5-page read_pages results and a full chapter for the summary.

probe:ocr-plan.summary:
I designed the OCR job and made no API calls. After splitting spreads there are 691 printed-page images. I checked the printed page numbers by eye for every PDF page. 2017: 142 PDF pages, 284 pages, printed 6–283 plus 6 unnumbered front pages. 2019: 178 PDF pages, 356 pages, printed 6–355 plus 6 front. 2003 제5장: 45 pages, printed 323–367 (printed = PDF page + 322). 2025 PDF pages 2–4: 6 pages, printed 2–7. 8 of these are blank end-of-chapter pages (confirmed by eye), so there are 683 requests.

Resolution: I chose 2000 px on the long edge for every page (1469×2000, 3,816 visual tokens each; the documented resize rule leaves it unchanged on Opus 5). At 1200 px the table digits are tight and the 2003 scan's running header is barely readable. 1600 px was readable everywhere, but 2000 px gives margin for exact table digits and the faint 2003 scan. It costs only about $2.4 more than 1600 px for the whole job.

Image-page input is better than PDF input: pages come as two-page spreads, the outlined glyphs have no text layer, and three 2019 files are 26–30 MB, which is about 35–40 MB once base64-encoded — over the 32 MB request limit.

All 683 requests serialize to 186.6 MB. That fits one batch (256 MB limit), but I recommend two batches (105 MB and 81 MB).

Cost (batch prices): $13.5–27.0, about 19–38k KRW. Add a pilot on the 12 check pages ($1.0–1.9) and re-runs (about $1). The design doc's 1.5–2만 원 matches only the low end. Output length drives the range: the Korean characters-per-token ratio and thinking tokens are still unknown.

Quality check: I typed 52 lines (1,613 characters) from the 2000 px images as ground truth. They cover 10 pages from 2017/2019 plus 2 extras (2003 scan, 2025). The error rate is the edit distance of each typed line against its best match in the page's transcript, divided by the typed characters. It is reported strict and normalized. Proposed pass bar: normalized error rate ≤1% on the 10 main pages with no wrong digit in tables, and ≤3% on the 2003 scan.

probe:search.summary:
Recommendation: search each printed page with character-bigram BM25 (bm25s 0.3.11, k1=1.5, b=0.75), not Kiwi. That flips the order in spec §4.1.

Installs: bm25s 0.3.11 (pure-Python wheel, needs only numpy; scipy and numba not needed), rank_bm25 0.2.2 and kiwipiepy 0.23.2 all installed cleanly as wheels on Windows / Python 3.12.10, with numpy 2.5.3. The exception is kiwipiepy_model 0.23.0, which has no wheel on PyPI, only an 88 MB source package. It builds without a compiler in 26 s. On manylinux, pip with --only-binary=:all: therefore fails.

Test setup:
- Corpus: 4,631 printed-page units from folders 2012-2016, 2018 and 2020-2025, 3.78M chars. Spreads were re-extracted with PyMuPDF and cut into left and right halves.
- Second run: the survey text as-is, one unit per PDF page (3,003 units).
- Space-lost test: the 2006 PyMuPDF text (no spaces) indexed together with the main set, and the same with 2006 re-extracted by pdfminer (spaces restored).
- Queries: 49 in eval_queries.jsonl (29 single facts, 5 multi-year, 5 broad topics, 10 on 2006). Each has a natural question and an assistant-style keyword string. A page counts as a correct target if it contains the query's key phrases (needle strings).

Main set, keyword query + year filter, Recall@5 / Recall@10:
| setup | R@5 / R@10 | peak RAM | build | query time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bigram | 99 / 99 (100 with years balanced) | 291 MB | 2 s | 0.2 ms |
| kiwi | 94 / 95 | 791 MB | 2.8 s on 24 threads, 30 s on one | 0.6 ms |
| kiwi_bi (one index with Kiwi tokens and bigrams) | 99 / 99 | 1,028 MB | 4.2 s | 0.6 ms |
| hybrid Kiwi + bigram, RRF fusion | 95 / 96 | 980 MB | 4.7 s | 1.2 ms |
| whitespace tokens | 82 / 90 | 168 MB | 1.2 s | 0.1 ms |

- Natural question + year filter: bigram 82/95, kiwi 85/95.
- Keyword query, no year filter: bigram 91/96, kiwi 85/90.
- 2006 space-lost text: bigram and Kiwi 90-100, whitespace tokens 0-40. Restoring spaces with pdfminer only helps the whitespace tokens (80-90).
- rank_bm25 gives similar recall but is 20-140x slower (12-28 ms per query).
- Changing k1 and b makes no difference: bigram stays at 99 R@10.

Hybrid is not proposed. kiwi_bi and hybrid tie bigram within one query and need 3.5x the RAM.

Failures found:
- Kiwi splits a short query differently from the same words in running text. The query "한일중 정상회의 서울 개최 2024" loses 한일중, so q25 and m04 miss.
- With a plain year filter over two years, the more-covered year fills the top 10 (m01). A balance_years option that interleaves each year's results fixes it.

Deliverables are in my folder: search_proto.py (build_index / search / save_index / load_index; the default is now bigram, and test_api.py passes), eval_queries.jsonl and results.md, which includes a short plain-Korean summary.

recommendations: Adopt character-bigram BM25 on bm25s (k1=1.5, b=0.75, method='lucene') with one document per printed page; change spec §4.1 to 'bigram by default' and close the §12 Kiwi/BM25 item. Do not add kiwipiepy to requirements.

Normalise both indexed text and queries with the prototype's clean(): NFC, ₩ to ·, middle-dot variants to ·, join PDF line breaks between Hangul syllables, 한·미·일 to 한미일. Reuse the same normaliser for the table/compare ✓/⚠ cell check.
Build the index in prep/ and save it with BM25.save() under corpus/index/ (about 13 MB for the main set). Load it at Space start (0.1 s). Keep page metadata in pages.jsonl.
search tool: always pass a year filter when the question names a year. When comparing 2-5 specific years, use balance_years=True (or one call per year) so each year is represented.
Tool description for Claude: retry with synonyms and word-order variants (한중일/한일중, 북미/미북, 사드/THAAD) when results look thin. Optionally add a small alias-expansion table.

Re-run the no-API search check (spec §8.1) on the real corpus/pages.jsonl once OCR for 2017/2019 and space recovery for the other folders are done. Add gold questions written by someone other than the query author.
Decide the search result snippet: the prototype shows about 150 chars around the first query match; the spec says the first 150 chars of the page.
risks: Eval bias: I chose the facts after reading the pages and wrote both the questions and the keywords. Keywords may reuse document wording, which favours exact word matching such as bigrams. With 49 queries, a difference of 2 queries or less is noise.
Correct-page sets from key phrases can be too strict (q18: only the page naming 센토사 counts) or loose (s10: 18 pages, b05: 13).
Wording variants (한중일 vs 한일중, 북미 vs 미북, 사드 vs THAAD) defeat any keyword index; the assistant has to reformulate.
Not tested: OCR text for 2017/2019, space-lost folders other than 2006 (2003-2005, 2007-2009, 2011, 참여정부), the ₩ fix on real 2008-2009 text, 참여정부 garbage running headers.
Year filter uses the covered year. Volumes also mention early events of the next year (the 2015 volume covers the Feb 2016 Kaesong shutdown), so a strict filter can hide valid pages.
Spreads were cut at the geometric middle; text crossing the gutter or wide tables may be split. The printed page numbers in the test corpus are estimates from the survey's page offsets.
Joining wrapped lines also merges some real boundaries at headings and table cells, adding a few junk bigrams.
bm25s get_scores([]) raises IndexError; the empty-query guard in the wrapper must stay.

If Kiwi is reintroduced later: 565 MB RAM for the model, an 88 MB source-only model package (--only-binary installs fail), num_workers=0 breaks batch tokenisation, and short queries can be split differently from the same words in running text.
Timings come from a 24-thread desktop. HF CPU Basic (2 vCPU) will be slower for multi-threaded Kiwi, but bigram indexing is already single-threaded (2 s).

probe:page-map-6.summary:
I built and checked the printed-page mapping for all six spread PDFs (folders 2020–2025). pdf_page N is 1-based (PyMuPDF index = N−1). Left half = printed 2N+k, right half = 2N+k+1. k = −4 for folders 2020 and 2021, and −2 for 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025. In 0-based form (i = N−1) the left half is 2i+(k+2), which gives −2 for 2020 and 2021 and 0 for 2022–2025.

**Page numbers.** k was taken by majority vote over outer-corner numbers near the top and bottom edges (2020 and 2025 print them at the bottom, 2021–2024 at the top). 1,966 of 1,980 detected page numbers agree with k (99.3%). Five volumes agree 100%; 2021 agrees 244 of 258 (94.6%). No roman numerals exist in any volume.

**Front matter.** It has no printed numbers, so its numbers come from k (label_source 'k'). Slots where 2N+k < 1 get printed_page None and label_source 'none': the cover spread in 2020 and 2021 (p1 plus p2L), and p1L in 2022–2025.

**Printed ranges** (every slot, by k / range of numbers actually printed):
- 2020: 1–377 / 8–375
- 2021: 1–281 / 7–279
- 2022: 1–345 / 8–343
- 2023: 1–396 / 8–395
- 2024: 1–386 / 10–383
- 2025: 1–341 / 8–339

Under k each volume is one consecutive, unique sequence. There is no separator page and no single page in the middle of any volume.

**Exceptions.**
1. 2021, PDF pages 5–11 (14 slots): the printed numbers read 007–020 where k gives 6–19. The book's own contents page and the chapter-1 divider both put 제1절 국제정세 개관 at 006, which is PDF 5L under k. Numbering matches k again from p13L (022).
2. Single-width last pages: 2023 p199 (colophon, 396) and 2024 p194 (no text, 386). Both are side 'L'.
3. Wider wrap covers: 2020 p1 and 2021 p1 (the latter has an offset crop box). For these two the cut moved to a word-free x because spine text crossed the middle.
4. 2025 has 24 image-only slots with no text: 2–7 in the front matter, plus 29–31, 57–59, 132–133, 174–175, 235–237, 262–263, 271–273.
5. Clip extraction glues a giant chapter numeral onto the previous word on 3 chapter-divider pages in 2023 ('기조1', '증진6', '활동7'). No character is lost.

**Split check.** Across 1,067 spread pages (404,416 words, 1,459,955 characters):
- 0 words and 0 text lines cross the cut.
- Line-assignment method (slot_text): 0 word or character mismatches.
- get_text(clip=...) method: 0 character mismatches; word mismatches only on the 3 glued 2023 pages above.
- Text blocks do cross the cut in 2020–2024, so text must never be split by block.

**Independent check.** Section-start pages (large '제N절' headings) were compared with the numbers printed on each book's contents and divider pages:
- 2020: 31 of 31
- 2021: 27 of 27 (the printed page numbers alone give 26 of 27)
- 2022: 28 of 28
- 2023: 27 of 27
- 2024: 28 of 28
- 2025: cannot be checked this way (its contents page is an image). It still has 100% page-number agreement over 314 slots.
- Off-by-one controls matched at most 1 page per volume.

**Confidence.** High for k, the clips and the ranges. Medium only for the choices about numbers that are not printed on the page: how to cite 2021 pages 6–19, and whether the title page counts as page 1.

I worked out the structure of all six volumes (folders 2020–2025) and wrote three deliverables: structure.json, toc.py (extract_toc, chapter_of) and notes.md.

**Per volume** (PDF pages → last printed page number; 장/절/부록 items; toc method):
- **2020** 「2021 외교백서」: 190 PDF pages → printed 375; 8/31/12; parsed from the text 목차 on PDF p4.
- **2021** 「2021년도 국제정세와 외교활동」: 142 → 279; 8/27/12; 목차 text, PDF p3.
- **2022** 「2022년도 …」: 173 → 343; 7/28/12; 목차 text, PDF p3.
- **2023** 「2023년도 …」: 199 → 395; 7/27/11; 목차 text, PDF p3.
- **2024** 「2024년도 …」: 194 → 383; 7/28/11; 목차 text, PDF p4.
- **2025** 「2025년도 …」: 171 → 339; 7/27/11; body headings plus running headers, because the 목차 is an image.

**TOC methods:**
- **(a) PDF outline** is useless everywhere. 2020 has only two file-merge bookmarks; 2021–2025 have none.
- **(b) 목차 text** parses in 2020–2024, including 2020's grid layout and 2021's numbers placed left of the labels.
- **(c) Body headings** alone recover every 절 and 부록 item in all six volumes.
  - Start pages match the printed 목차 everywhere except one entry in 2021.
  - Titles match after normalisation (spaces, punctuation, dot variants).
  - 2025 was checked against my own visual transcription of its image 목차: 38/38 correct.
- **Final toc** uses the 목차 titles (2020–2024), but each 절 start page is the page where its heading actually appears.

**Chapter lookup:** a 장 starts on its unnumbered divider page (간지). I checked chapter_of against the running header of every numbered page:
- 장: 1,980/1,980 agree.
- 절 (pages whose header names a 절): 986/986 agree.
- 20 edge-case tests pass.

**Missing registry (12 entries):**
- 2025 인사말: PDF p2, printed 2–3, image.
- 2025 목차: PDF p3, printed 4–5, image.
- 2025 dividers, all images: p4, 16, 30, 67, 88, 119, 132, 137 → printed 6–7, 30–31, 58–59, 132–133, 174–175, 236–237, 262–263, 272–273.
- 2025 부록 1 조직도: PDF p138, printed 274–275; the chart is an image.
- 2021 인사말: the posted PDF has none; printed range left null.
- No gaps in printed page numbers in any volume. corpus_years = 2020–2025.

**Key new finding:** 2021's page offset is not constant.
- PDF p5–11 carry printed 7–20 with odd numbers on the left, i.e. 2N−3.
- PDF p12 is a full-spread divider that can only be printed 21.
- PDF p13–141 follow 2N−4.
- As a result, 목차 says 제1장 제1절 starts on 006, but the heading sits on the page numbered 007. I store 7 and keep toc_page 6 in the entry.

Fix the design spec: 2025 PDF p2 = 인사말, p3 = 목차, p4 = 제1장 divider. Seven more dividers (p16/30/67/88/119/132/137) and the 부록 1 조직도 (p138) are also image-only.

probe:extract-text-6.summary:
Text extraction for all 2,138 halves (1,069 PDF pages) of the 2020-2025 volumes is decided and checked.

**Method**
- PyMuPDF rawdict, clipped at the page midline, kept in content-stream order. sort=True is not used.
- Two order fixes: big titles move up, footnotes move to the end.
- Header, footer and side-tab bands are learned per volume.
- Visual lines are joined into paragraphs using the trailing-space signal.
- Output: extract.py, which needs running_strings.json next to it; quality.csv; notes.md.

**Spacing quality**
All volumes are clean, so no fallback engine was needed.

| Year | Long-run share raw / clean | 1-syllable share raw / clean | Halves flagged |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2020 | 0.013% / 0.015% | 9.6% / 5.7% | 0 |
| 2021 | 0.018% / 0.030% | 8.8% / 4.7% | 0 |
| 2022 | 0.022% / 0.026% | 9.2% / 5.4% | 0 |
| 2023 | 0.023% / 0.026% | 9.0% / 5.2% | 1 |
| 2024 | 0.022% / 0.024% | 9.3% / 5.5% | 1 |
| 2025 | 0.015% / 0.016% | 6.4% / 5.5% | 0 |

- Long run = 13 or more Hangul syllables with no space.
- The 2 flagged halves (2023 p165 R, 2024 p161 R) are tables of organisation names. Every long run in all six volumes is a real compound name.
- Cleaned text without whitespace: 247,657 / 195,171 / 227,920 / 268,800 / 257,370 / 218,347 characters.

**Header and footer rules**
- Header y0: 2020 = 43, 2021 = 46, 2022 = 27, 2023 = 31, 2024 = 31, 2025 = 49.
- Page numbers sit in the header in 2021-2024 and in a footer in 2020 (y0 639) and 2025 (y0 654).
- Side tabs are in the 50 pt outer margin of the right half in 2020-2024. In 2025 the tab is not text.
- extract_half_text puts running blocks first and last. clean_text strips them only if every line is a learned running string and the volume's pattern holds: footer and tab only after a header; header and footer always together in 2020/2025; a page number in the header in 2021-2024.
- The text rule and the geometric roles agree on all 2,138 halves.

**Reading order**
- Default order is kept. Prose goes upward in only 4 halves after the fixes (2020 p31 L, p77 L, p126 L; 2022 p147 R).
- Tables come out one cell per line, row by row. Photo captions follow their paragraph.
- Title and footnote fixes changed 50, 47, 49, 55, 51 and 6 halves.
- Org-chart vertical glyphs are merged into words.

**Paragraph joining**
- Mid-word breaks joined: 2365/2372, 1634/1650, 1998/1999, 2429/2432, 2259/2261, 3/3. The leftovers are table-of-contents entries that should stay separate.
- A sentence end without a trailing space always starts a new paragraph (0 joined).
- No new glued sentences and no headings glued to body text.

**Normalisation**
- Middle-dot variants become the standard dot, including one private-use Wingdings glyph (2025 p43) and the half-width forms common in 2025.
- InDesign control characters \x07 and \x08 are removed.
- Soft hyphens (2023/2024) are removed and the word re-joined. A hard '-' at line end is always a real hyphen (14 cases) and is kept.
- Glyph gaps over 0.5 em become spaces (4-13 lines per volume). This fixes merged table cells like 2025 p50 '면담한-CARICOM'.
- Letter-spaced labels ('양 자 관 계') are collapsed.

**Image-only halves**
- Real content lost as images: 2025 p2 L+R (인사말), p3 L+R (목차), p138 L+R (조직도). The survey's "PDF 2-4" is slightly off: p4 is the Chapter 1 divider.
- Decorative chapter dividers:
  - 2025 p4, 16, 30, 67, 88, 119, 132, 137 (both halves)
  - 2020 p5, 15, 29, 49, 97, 113, 132, 156, 162 L
  - 2021 p4, 12, 18, 31, 58, 74, 91, 110 R
- Covers: 2020 p1 L, p2 R; 2021 p1 R, p2 R.
- Also found: 35 blank halves and 24 title-only halves.

**Runtime**
- extract + clean for all halves takes 0.56-0.94 s per volume.
- The whole pipeline for all six volumes takes 15.0 s: profiling, extract+clean, find_image_only and the one-off build_running_strings (3.5 s).

**Residual problems**
- Table-of-contents pages come out grouped by style, with page numbers separated from their entries.
- Table rows are implicit.
- Display digits on 2022 openers come out in pieces.
- Cover spine text is duplicated in both halves.
- 2021 page numbering is not a single k (see risks).

recommendations: In prep/, use: text = clean_text(extract_half_text(pdf, n, side), year). Copy extract.py and running_strings.json together. Rebuild running_strings.json with build_running_strings() if the PDFs change.

Store method='text' for all halves except the 6 content-image halves: 2025 p2 L/R, p3 L/R, p138 L/R. Register those in missing.json (or OCR them in phase 2). Mark decorative chapter dividers and blank halves as empty pages rather than missing content.

Page-map task: do not assume a single k for 2021. Header numbers give k=-3 on PDF p5-p11 and k=-4 from p13, with the p12 chapter-2 opener holding only printed page 021. Detect k per half from quality.csv header_text / footer_text.
Use the cleaned one-paragraph-per-line text for the bigram/Kiwi BM25 index. Line joining removes about 4 points of 1-syllable fragments, e.g. '한·아' + '세안' becomes '한·아세안'.

Glyph-gap spacing (>0.5 em) adds spaces to letter-spaced decorative text on 2020 chapter openers ('외 교 백 서').
